Native DF 53.16 adventure introduction construction
==================================================

This is a static source reconstruction from the two PE files configured in
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. No game code was run. The adjacent .asm
files preserve the complete native instructions, including conditional edges;
this text names the branches that construct displayed introduction text.

Disassembler: fixed native w64devkit-2.9.1/w64devkit/bin/objdump.exe, Intel x64.

Reference entry / unwind range: 0x1407E6840 .. 0x1407EB3C4.
Reference executable return: 0x1407EB332.
Reference embedded jump tables begin at 0x1407EB334; objdump's subsequent
"(bad)" lines describe embedded data, not extra text construction branches.
Classic entry / unwind range: 0x1407E40C0 .. 0x1407E8C44.
Classic equivalent instruction addresses in this function are reference
addresses minus 0x2780. Strings have independent image coordinates.

The function first creates/restores the requested adventurers and their party.
The complete initialization branches remain in reference-introduction.asm and
classic-introduction.asm. Narrative construction starts at 0x1407EA2B6 only
when the start-site pointer at [rbp+0x108] is present. It constructs:

  main_text   = std::string at [rbp+0x370]
  vault_text  = std::string at [rbp+0x390]
  temporary  = std::string at [rbp+0x3D0]
  party       = vector at [rbp+0xA8], including the protagonist
  local_party = vector at [rbp+0xC0]
  protagonist = unit pointer at [rbp-0x40]
  origin      = corresponding input descriptor pointer at [rbp+0x8]
  start_site  = pointer from input vector's [+0x18] site id

local_party selects input descriptors whose [+0x340] matches start_site[+0x88]
and whose [+0x2D0] is not -1, and retains the corresponding created unit.

Displayed text branch reconstruction
------------------------------------

1. Siege prefix (0x1407EA3B9 .. 0x1407EA67E)

   Iterate protagonist[+0x10]->[+0x130]->[+0x40]->[+0x68] event vector.
   Select the first event satisfying all of:
     event discriminator (0x1400BBB20) == 0
     event[+0x00] != protagonist[+0x10][+0xB0]
     event validity helper 0x140072D10(current year/current tick) == true
     event[+0x04] == start_site[+0x88]
     event[+0x04] == origin[+0x340]
   If event's site id lookup (0x14007DB20) fails, continue to bandit path.

   Append "The peaceful town of " + site-name(site) +
          " is threatened!  The forces of ".
   If event[+0x08] != -1:
     append histfig-description(event[+0x08], default context, grammar=0,
                                 noun mode=0).
   Else append "darkness".
   Append " are on the march.  ".
   If event[+0x0C] != -1:
     append "Commanded by " + histfig-description(event[+0x0C], ...) + ", they".
   Else append "The enemy".
   Append " will have no mercy.  There is little time -- you must flee.  Perhaps your family and friends can be convinced to leave."

   Thus the two independent id-present/id-absent decisions produce four siege
   text combinations. The first dynamic figure is the force description and
   the second is its commander. These are both historical-figure formatter
   calls, rather than an entity-name formatter followed by a person formatter.
   The reviewed siege template therefore uses {e} for the town and {p} for
   the invading historical figure; an entity-typed {e} in the second slot
   would reject the same caste/curse/name forms as the bandit leader.
   A selected siege does not also append the bandit prefix.

2. Optional vault paragraph (0x1407EA67E .. 0x1407EABA2)

   This follows only the selected siege with event[+0x08] != -1. Resolve that
   historical figure. Require its [+0x130]->[+0x58] and that object's [+0x50]
   bit 0. Iterate world[+0x178] sites and select candidates with:
     site[+0x80] == 10
     site[+0x310] != null
     site[+0x310][+0x02] == 1
     site[+0x310][+0x2C] == the figure's [+0xE0] id
   Search the world structure collection at 0x1424E7E98, each [+0x28] vector,
   and retain an element for which type helper 0x140072930 returns 1.
   If none exists, do not build this paragraph.

   vault_text = "Legends speak of "
   if structure[+0x04] == -1: append "an ancient"
   else: append "a"
   append " vault, " + site-reference(site[+0x88], flags=0) + ", where "
   append histfig-description(figure[+0xE0], default context, grammar=0,
                              noun mode=0)
   append " wrested "
   pronoun = 0x140AA4850(figure[+0x06], capitalize=false)
   append pronoun + " power from the Underworld by invoking " + pronoun
   append " true name.  The location of this place is well-known, but none have penetrated its secrets.  If the true name of the monster can be uncovered, you might be able to end this terror forever."

   Pronoun branches: sex==1 -> "his"; sex==0 -> "her"; other -> "its".
   Both pronoun occurrences reuse the same constructed string. Article x sex
   gives six possible forms. No second person or second independent pronoun.
   This code also registers the site information for party members, without
   appending additional introduction prose.

3. Bandit prefix (0x1407EABAF .. 0x1407EADDD)

   Reached when no siege was selected. Require origin, origin[+0x340] != -1,
   protagonist and its event vector described above. Select first event with:
     event discriminator == 6
     event[+0x00] != the active unit's [+0x10][+0xB0]
     event[+0x04] == origin[+0x340]
     event validity helper == true
   Resolve the event[+0x04] site; if absent, skip this prefix.

   append "The citizens of " + site-name(site)
   append " are plagued by bandits.  The gang"
   if event[+0x08] != -1:
     append " led by " + histfig-description(event[+0x08], default context,
                                             grammar=0, noun mode=0)
   append " has even sent some troublemakers to harass people right here in town."

   This yields the leader-present and leader-absent forms. The leader-present
   dynamic field can be "the human necromancer <name>", as in the screenshot.

4. Shared main body (0x1407EADE2 .. 0x1407EB082)

   If main_text is nonempty, append the literal "  ".
   P = party.size(); L = local_party.size().
   local_index = 0x1400BA600(protagonist, local_party).

   if local_index == -1 and L != 0:
     if P >= 3:
       append "Just reunited after a long journey, you are together with your companions again.  "
     else:
       append "After a long journey, you are here to meet your most trusted companion.  "
     Choose one random local_party unit using 0x140071F30(L).
     If chosen_unit[+0x10][+0x38] is nonempty:
       copy that string, capitalize via 0x14052D650, append it.
     Else:
       append histfig-description(chosen_unit[+0x10][+0xE0], default context,
                                  grammar=0, noun mode=1).
     append " is from here and might have some local information."
   else if origin exists and
           (origin[+0x2D0] != -1 or local_index != -1):
     if P >= 3:
       if P == L:
         append "Your most trusted local companions are meeting you here today."
       else:
         append "Your most trusted companions have made the journey to meet you here today."
     else if P >= 2:
       if P == L:
         append "After a long journey, you are here to meet your most trusted companion."
       else:
         append "Your most trusted companion has made the journey to meet you here today."
     else:
       append "You've finally got your equipment together, such as it is.  Now it's time for action and adventure!  "
       append "In the rush of excitement, you've forgotten where you were going to go."
   else:
     if P >= 3:
       append "Just reunited after a long journey, you are together with your companions again.  "
     else if P >= 2:
       append "After a long journey, you are here to meet your most trusted companion.  "
     else:
       append "Your wanderings have brought you to this place after a long journey."

5. Rescue suffix (0x1407EB087 .. 0x1407EB174)

   Iterate protagonist's same event vector and count entries with discriminator
   == 1. The native code accumulates this count in r14d/ebx.
   count==0: no rescue text.
   count==1: append "  A foolhardy soul might try to rescue the child that has been kidnapped."
   count>1: append "  A foolhardy soul might try to rescue the children that have been kidnapped."
   rescued_hint_present is true only when one of the last two forms was added.

6. Final suffix (0x1407EB177 .. 0x1407EB1E2)

   if P >= 2:
     append "  Let the party venture forth!"
   else if origin exists and
           (origin[+0x2D0] != -1 or local_index != -1):
     if rescued_hint_present:
       append "  Perhaps some of your friends here have ideas."
     else:
       append "  Perhaps some of your friends here can remind you."
   else:
     append "  Perhaps some of the people here will be worth talking to before you continue on your way."

7. Submission and both visible consumers

   0x1407EB1E7 constructs announcement options: kind 0x008F, color 7,
   attribute byte 1, duration 2000. 0x1407EB225 submits main_text through
   0x1400E3C20 with global 0x1424E3850. If vault_text is nonempty,
   0x1407EB273 submits it separately with the same options.

   Dispatch 0x1400E3C20 .. 0x1400E569D copies submitted text into native
   announcement objects at 0x1400E4330 .. 0x1400E4352, whose queued pointer
   vector is 0x1424E3880 / 0x1424E3888. It also submits to the native text
   object at 0x1424E3898 via 0x140D51EB0.
   The current announcement popup consumes this queue independently of help.
   Full renderer sources: reference-popup-render.asm,
   0x1400E9F40 .. 0x1400EA4C8; classic-popup-render.asm,
   0x1400E9ED0 .. 0x1400EA458. Classic dispatch is preserved separately in
   classic-message-dispatch.asm, 0x1400E3BB0 .. 0x1400E562D. Its queue vector
   is 0x1424DD770 / 0x1424DD778 and richbox is 0x1424DD788.

   Dispatch tests per-announcement flags bit 0 at 0x1400E4303 before queuing.
   It copies the submitted full NativeString into the queued entry, then
   clears/rebuilds the richbox from queue[0] at 0x1400E43BF .. 0x1400E43D9.
   0x1400E43EA calls word layout with width 50 (0x32). Classic equivalent
   rebuild/layout calls are 0x1400E4369 (0x140D4EEF0) and 0x1400E437A
   (0x140D4ECC0). Complete word layout sources: reference-popup-layout.asm,
   0x140D51C80 .. 0x140D51EAB; classic-popup-layout.asm,
   0x140D4ECC0 .. 0x140D4EEEB. These functions end at RET, preserving their
   split unwind-region continuations rather than stopping after the prologue.
   It preserves punctuation words and controls; regular words receive x/y
   fields at +0x28/+0x2C. Layout uses richbox +0x30 as current width and
   +0x34 as last occupied row, both independent of the source string length.

   Popup renderer branches:
     - Empty queue -> return, with no popup body or confirmation label.
     - Frame X = midpoint(incoming left/right) - 26, right = frame X + 53.
       Frame Y = init.display.grid_y / 2 - (richbox.max_y + 8) / 2,
       calculated at 0x1400E9F9C .. 0x1400E9FB1. The height becomes at
       least 10 when graphics mode and manager[+0x88] portrait id != -1.
     - Graphics + valid portrait id reserves portrait space: frame left
       moves 6 columns left, frame right 6 columns right. Text origin is
       frame left + 14; the ordinary text origin is frame left + 2.
       Both use frame top + 2 plus each word's own coordinates.
     - Every richbox word is drawn directly from its own NativeString,
       using RGB bytes +0x20/+0x21/+0x22 and use_old_16_colors=0.
       0x1400EA17C calls 0x140AD9960 (addst), with the word in RDX and
       R9D=0. Classic equivalent is 0x1400EA10C -> 0x140AD69A0.
       The full announcement is never sent through add_paragraph here.
     - Portrait drawing additionally requires successful historical-figure
       lookup, its graphics data, available portrait index, and figure flag
       bit 2; failures skip only that drawing, without changing body text.
     - The three-row button below the body uses queue size: >1 creates
       "More" with immediate 0x65726F4D at 0x1400EA417; otherwise "Okay"
       with immediate 0x79616B4F at 0x1400EA440. Classic equivalents are
       0x1400EA3A7 / 0x1400EA3D0. popup-literal-sources.tsv retains these
       immediate-string origins. No other prose branch exists in renderer.

   Help initializer 0x1401F5A6D .. 0x1401F5AB7 also iterates that queue, appends
   every full submitted string to its paragraph buffer, then appends "[B]".
   Thus prefixes, main body, rescue and final suffix already share one string;
   the optional vault paragraph is separately queued. Popup displays the first
   queued entry's own word layout; help combines queued entries as paragraphs.

   The supplied screenshot selects the single local-origin adventurer branch:
     0x1407EB01B equipment/action literal (classic 0x1407E889B),
     0x1407EB02E forgotten destination literal (classic 0x1407E88AE),
     0x1407EB1CB friends/reminder ending (classic 0x1407E8A4B).
   There is no rescue, siege, bandit or vault prose in that captured string.
   All three are already members of the 29 semantic source entries below.

8. Exceptional start-site path (0x1407EA1B2 .. 0x1407EA2B1)

   If start_site is absent, ask world helper 0x140F77F10 for a starting square.
   If the returned square id is -1, the native code calls MessageBoxW and then
   exits. Its two UTF-16LE sources are:
     title: "FATAL ERROR"
       reference RVA 0x16ABA48, file 0x16AAC48
       classic RVA 0x16A60B8, file 0x16A4EB8
     message: "Could not locate adventure start square"
       reference RVA 0x16AD410, file 0x16AC610
       classic RVA 0x16A8600, file 0x16A7400
   Neither has final punctuation. Their ASCII first-byte readings "F" and
   "C" are not full strings. If a square exists, the no-site path initializes
   travel/map state and skips the prose construction above.

Dynamic historical-figure formatter
----------------------------------

Full source: reference-histfig-description.asm, 0x140B92F10 .. 0x140B93927.
Default context constructor: reference-histfig-format-context.asm,
0x140072080 .. 0x14007216D (leaf function without its own unwind entry).

The introduction invokes the default context, with [+0x00]=0, [+0x08]=null,
[+0x10]=null, [+0x20]=[+0x24]=-1, grammar=0. Most calls use noun mode 0.
Local companion fallback uses noun mode 1, suppressing extra species text.

Default-call reachable text branches:
  - Failed historical-figure lookup: "an unknown creature".
  - Figure has a name: either its formatted language name alone, or
    "the " + optional "zombie " + optional "ghostly " + caste/race noun +
    optional special descriptor + " " + formatted language name.
  - Figure has no name: "a " + optional "zombie " + optional "ghostly " +
    caste/race noun + optional special descriptor.
  - Descriptive noun is suppressed for invalid race, explicit noun mode 1,
    contextual same-race figures or certain figure flags; the named form
    becomes just the formatted name.
  - [+0x130]->[+0x48][+0x160] supplies the zombie condition.
  - [+0xC8] first flag byte sign-bit supplies ghostly when special descriptor
    [+0x130]->[+0x48][+0x88] is not active.
  - [+0x130]->[+0x48][+0x88] enables the appended special description stored
    as a native string at [+0x90], including dynamically assigned professions
    or supernatural titles such as necromancer.
  - Named descriptive noun selects caste raw [+0x20] first, falls back to
    race raw [+0x20]; both come from raw vector 0x1424ECA68/0x1424ECA70.
  - Unnamed noun uses 0x140AA3BD0 (reference-creature-noun.asm), same caste
    singular / race singular fallback. Invalid raw indices can yield empty
    nouns; there is no hidden extra unknown label in that helper.

Additional formatter branches retained in the full disassembly but not selected
by the default introduction context/arguments:
  - Context [+0x08] metadata restricts identity: "interrogator", "subject",
    known name, "Nameless", or "an unidentified creature".
  - Context [+0x24] equal to the figure id uses grammar-dependent "I", "me",
    "my", "myself". The short strings I/me/my use immediate little-endian
    stores 0x49, 0x656D, 0x796D, and myself copies six bytes at 0x141662EF8.
  - Noun mode 2 can produce <name> + " the " + descriptive creature text.
  - Grammar 2 appends "'s" unless "my" already supplied the possessive.
  - Context flags bit 1 wraps an id with "[LPAGE:HF:" + "]" / "[/LPAGE]".
  - Context [+0x20] can change the name to its familiar form or the unnamed
    indefinite article from "a " to "the ".

Dynamic site and language-name sources
--------------------------------------

site-name: reference-site-name.asm, 0x140A94030 .. 0x140A946D1.
vault site-reference: reference-vault-site-reference.asm,
0x140B93930 .. 0x140B93A8A. Missing site lookup appends "an unknown site";
flags bit 1 optionally adds [LPAGE:SITE:id] markup, but intro passes flags 0.
Language name: reference-language-name.asm, 0x140A946E0 .. 0x140A94EA2.
Names use native first-name/nickname strings and language word ids [+0x40]
through [+0x58], with parts returned by 0x140D2CB50. Besides explicit spaces,
native construction can append "The ", "the ", "Of ", "of ", nickname quotes
using immediate bytes 0x60 (`) and 0x27 ('), and a hyphen using immediate byte
0x2D at 0x140A94C79. These are name grammar, not missing introduction prose.

The adjacent *-literal-sources.tsv files retain exact native constituent
locations. help-sources.tsv retains semantic sentence templates, including all
siege, bandit, companion, rescue, ending and six vault forms above. Its "a vault"
article provenance is corrected to PE:file:0x1601FB4, the actual introduction
RIP target 0x141602DB4, rather than accidental PE-header occurrence 0x265.

Translation consumers
---------------------

The 29 semantic source entries in help-sources.tsv comprise 15 shared-body,
companion, rescue and ending entries, four siege entries, three bandit entries
and seven vault entries (six article/pronoun forms plus the shared tail).
help-translations.tsv retains the Chinese prose for each; fortress_help.inc
combines covered fragments into the complete native paragraph. Those entries
are generated as help rules, not general UI-message literal rules. The live
announcement popup previously called translate_complete_announcement, whose
UI-message-only literal/grammar route could not consume these help entries.
Its existing complete source ownership and word layout were therefore not
enough to translate the screenshot's fixed three-part introduction string.

announcement_translation.inc now tries the same reviewed help paragraph
coverage (ui_message=false) on each complete native announcement block after the
reviewed UI-message literal and before recursive combat/dialogue parsing.
This consumes the entire source only when every constituent and typed slot
is covered. It reaches all 29 shared-body/siege/bandit/vault entries, including
the same historical-figure grammar used by the help consumer; it does not
match individual screen rows or install screenshot-specific fragments.

All help {p} fields now resolve complete native person/deity identities through
the native identity source table, then the shared historical-actor grammar.
The original captured span is retained for authored nicknames, and the existing
unit identity parser accepts authored Chinese names in this proved person slot.
This includes invading figures, commanders, bandit leaders, vault figures and
local companions; race/caste, zombie, ghostly and stored supernatural descriptors
remain separate from the generated name rather than being phoneticized as names.

The two exceptional UTF-16LE MessageBoxW sources are handled separately by
native_adventure_introduction.inc because they bypass SDL paragraph drawing:
"FATAL ERROR" -> "致命错误";
"Could not locate adventure start square" -> "无法找到冒险起始方格".
The installed-memory literal replacements retain each original byte extent and
are restored on core detach. The on-disk executable is not changed.
